A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MS-IMAP work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and figures, tables, equations, and relocated material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering experiments on synthetic and real datasets, feature-importance results, hyperparameter analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical experiments and adds Cora evaluation, additional comparisons, and feature-selection performance curves.

M1.justification: v3 removes the proposed edge-betweenness-centrality/KDE sampling component and adds mutual-information feature scoring using k-means pseudo-labels (Section 6 and Appendix 9). The underlying SGW tensor encoding, optimization loss, and summation across scales remain equivalent. Concatenation Method 1 is retained in Appendix 8.

E1.justification: v3 adds Cora's citation-document features, explicitly excluding its supplied graph edges. Feature-importance evaluation shifts from the AwA example to Cora and Zilionis. Census, Zilionis, AwA, noisy two moons, and dense-sparse synthetic clustering remain covered.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds PHATE and raw-feature clustering comparisons. ISOMAP and Diffusion Maps also join the primary real-dataset comparison, whereas v1 reported their real-data results only in appendix parameter studies. This substantially broadens the main comparator set.

E3.justification: Feature-importance evaluation changes from an AwA score plot to clustering across retained feature counts, with original-space controls and LS-versus-MI comparisons on Cora and Zilionis. This introduces a substantial evaluation design. Main clustering retains k-means, ARI, and AMI; newly disclosed baseline settings alone do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v3 Figures 1 and 3–5 test whether selected features preserve clustering quality and how LS, MI, and original versus embedded features differ. These analyses replace v1's AwA ranking illustration. Existing noise, density, neighbor-count, filter-count, and baseline-parameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 first reports five runs per hyperparameter configuration for UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE, and HeatGeo, with averaging before selecting the best configuration. v1 does not disclose repeated-run counts. No dispersion estimates or confidence intervals are added, and an actual increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Primary scores and rankings change: Census UMAP ARI/AMI moves from 0.05/0.08 in v1 Table 2 to 0.23/0.15 in v3 Table 1, tying MS-IMAP. New Cora, PHATE, raw-feature, and feature-selection results appear. Method 1 disappears from primary comparisons but remains in the dense-sparse experiment. Changed tuning reporting limits same-setting performance interpretations.

T1.justification: Appendix 17 adds two Laplacian-power lemmas, replaces the proof of Theorem 3, and introduces Corollary 1. It also adds an energy-constrained derivation of supposedly optimal multiscale coefficients in Equations 19–25. The principal uniqueness-set theorem statements are largely retained.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the novel network-sampling contribution with feature interpretability, which v1 described as outside its main focus. The conclusion now emphasizes two unsupervised/self-supervised importance methods. The broad multiscale embedding and Paley-Wiener representation claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains that LS neighborhood preservation need not imply cluster discrimination and that MI depends on pseudo-label quality. It removes the AwA interpretation that roughly ten high-scoring attributes capture most information. The general geodesic-distance, out-of-sample, and global-versus-local limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix 12 adds explicit UMAP, t-SNE, and PHATE search grids. Cora documentation specifies 2,708 publications, 1,433 features, and exclusion of supplied edges. Existing hardware, runtime, and Chebyshev-computation details are retained; these disclosures do not themselves prove changed settings for earlier experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for geometric scattering, PHATE, Cora, and heat-based signatures. Its positioning more explicitly acknowledges existing higher-dimensional graph representations. The broader related-work discussion and most cited works remain.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: preliminaries become related-work subsections, Method 1 moves to the appendix, the main method focuses on tensor encoding, feature importance is rewritten, and conclusions become a separate Discussion section. Abstract and introductory explanations are also revised.

P2.justification: The two primary result tables merge into an expanded table. New feature-selection plots replace the AwA score plot, the EBC diagram disappears, and the feature-correspondence diagram moves to the appendix. Additional tuning tables and revised algorithm displays substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical scrutiny through broader tuned comparisons and controlled feature-selection curves, replacing v1's isolated AwA score illustration. However, the new Appendix 17 coefficient-optimality argument has correctness problems: its proposed allocation is not generally optimal under the stated constraint, and Equation 25 omits the normalization factor implied by Equations 19 and 24. These empirical gains coexist with a new defect in a central theoretical contribution, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
